source.title: Demystifying Data Organization for Enhanced LLM Training
source.authors: Yalun Dai; Yang-Yu Huang; Tong Yang; Yonghan Wang; Xin Zhang; Wenshan Wu; Qi-Hao Zhao; Hao Li; Yuan-Yuan Gao; Kim-Hui Yap; Scarlett Li

record.tranche_reason: The study fits a parameter-and-token scaling law to held-out language-model test losses from its own pretraining runs, using the Chinchilla scaling-law form.
record.gate_note: The study reports fits and goodness-of-fit values for DCLM test loss, plus a figure comparing test-loss trajectories across model sizes and data-ordering strategies. Its GPT-3 and Llama-family losses are extrapolated estimates, not evaluations on runs of those sizes, so they do not validate large-run prediction. Downstream benchmark scores and cited scaling-law results are not rows for the claim.
record.test_reason: Appendix D fits the Chinchilla joint form L(N,D)=E+A/N^α+B/D^β to the study's own held-out DCLM test losses (80 points; 160M–1.7B, 2.5B–50B tokens) and reports R² goodness of fit. This is a narrow-range check of V1. The fit's main use is as a tool to extrapolate data-ordering gains.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors say the fitted Chinchilla-form curves fit the size and token effects very well (high R²). They use the fit to extrapolate that ordering gains persist at GPT-3 and Llama scales. The paper's main conclusion is that the four data-organization guidances and the STR/SAW orderings improve training stability and performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the Chinchilla-style joint loss form, but fits its own DCLM test-loss curves with a two-stage initialization followed by Huber-loss LBFGS optimization; the study focuses on data ordering and fits curves for its own training runs.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that LBFGS was sensitive to parameter initialization and use a two-stage fitting procedure to address this. The fitted constants also vary across the Random, STR, and SAW data-ordering setups.

fits_no_version.finding: STR and SAW orderings give lower DCLM test loss than random ordering at all four model sizes (Figure 7, figure only).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Score-based data ordering lowers held-out pretraining loss across model sizes.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The scaling fit covers four model sizes from 160M to 1.7B and up to 50B training tokens, not several orders of magnitude in parameter count. The extrapolated larger-model estimates are not checked against observed runs. Figure 7 provides no numerical loss values in the text, and the scaling-fit constants have no reported uncertainty intervals.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted due to the 60-row limit. Table 7's GPT-3 and Llama-family entries are extrapolated predictions rather than observed outcomes, so they were not recorded as validated extrapolation results.

untested.parts: Compute axis; ranges of several orders of magnitude (N spans about 10x, D about 20x); non-bottleneck conditions.
Table 7 extrapolations to GPT-3 and Llama scale are never checked against observed losses.
Only text pretraining is fitted; no scaling fit for SFT.
Downstream averages rise with model size (Table 6), but no predictive fit to scale or loss is made.
Alternative fitting methods, parameter counting and schedules are not compared quantitatively, nor is curvature away from a power law assessed.

missing.what: Authors report that the LBFGS fit is sensitive to initialization and adopt a two-stage initialization. This is qualitative evidence of fit-method dependence; no alternative-fit numbers are given.
Downstream average accuracy rises monotonically with model size, e.g. Random FW 40.52→47.72 from 160M to 1.7B. Relevant context, though no predictability test is made.

record.verdict_notes: The scaling-law fit is a side analysis serving a data-ordering paper. The V1 support is narrow: four sizes, up to 50B tokens, about one order of magnitude per axis. The R² values are partly circular because they are computed after subtracting the fitted terms. Table 7 extrapolations are predictions only and do not test V2. The peer-review venue in the record (ACL) is not stated in the text given.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test scaling with compute, establish the non-bottleneck conditions, or cover several orders of magnitude in parameter count.
The large-model losses are extrapolated estimates, with no observed losses from the extrapolated runs to assess prediction accuracy.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation is measured.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
The study concerns language-model pretraining and SFT, not other modalities or the other listed training regimes.
The study reports downstream scores but does not test their predictability from scale or pretraining loss.
It does not compare alternative fitting methods or parameter-counting conventions, test compute-optimal splits, or assess whether curves bend away from a power law.

rows.subject: Mistral-architecture pretraining runs (160M, 470M, 1B, and 1.7B)
rows.operation_detail: Fit the stated joint parameter-and-token scaling law to DCLM test losses from runs trained from 0B to 50B tokens.
rows.measure: Fitted constants (A, B, α, β, E)
rows.note: Fit used 80 (model size, token count, loss) tuples.
rows.check: The fitted constants alone do not show whether loss follows a power law; fit quality is in r4–r18. Across orderings, α differs by only 0.007 and β by 0.007, with no uncertainty reported. E is identical (1.693) in all three fits. So it cannot be read as setup-dependence of exponents.

relationships.condition: Mistral models 160M–1.7B, 2.5B–50B tokens, DCLM held-out loss, under Random, STR and SAW ordering
relationships.reason: Chinchilla-form fit gives R² 0.992–0.999 per model size along tokens (r4–r15) and 0.999 along size (r16–r18). The range is only about one order of magnitude per axis.
relationships.display_finding: Chinchilla-form fits achieve R²=0.992–0.999 along tokens and 0.999 along model size over about one order of magnitude per axis.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
